text: Presidential elections were held in Ghana on 3 November 1992, marking the first contested elections since 1979 and only the fourth contested elections since the country gained independence in 1957. Jerry Rawlings, who had led the country since seizing power in a 1981 coup, had reluctantly agreed to hold multiparty elections earlier that year. He ran as the candidate of the Progressive Alliance, which included his National Democratic Congress, and secured 58.4% of the vote, winning without the need for a runoff. Voter turnout was 50.2%. The opposition claimed that Rawlings and his supporters committed widespread fraud, such as ballot-box stuffing and altering certified results, but international observers declared the elections to be free and fair.
